title: Understanding the Project Structure
overview: When you create a React Native CLI project, several folders and files are generated automatically. Each folder has a specific purpose, such as storing source code, native Android and iOS projects, dependencies, and configuration files. Understanding the project structure helps you organize your application effectively.

example.title: Default Project Structure
example.content:
MyApp/
├── android/
├── ios/
├── node_modules/
├── App.tsx
├── index.js
├── package.json
└── metro.config.js

title: The android Folder
overview: The android folder contains the complete native Android project. It includes Gradle files, AndroidManifest.xml, Java or Kotlin source files, resources, and everything required to build and run the Android application.

example.title: Important Android Files
example.content:
android/
├── app/
├── gradle/
├── build.gradle
├── settings.gradle
└── gradlew

title: The ios Folder
overview: The ios folder contains the native iOS project. It includes Xcode project files, Swift or Objective-C source files, CocoaPods configuration, and everything required to build the application for iPhone and iPad devices.

title: App.tsx
overview: App.tsx is the main component of a React Native application. It acts as the root component where your application's UI begins. In larger projects, it usually contains the navigation container or the main screen of the application.

example.title: Basic App.tsx

title: index.js
overview: The index.js file is the application's entry point. It registers the root component with React Native so the application knows which component should be loaded when it starts.

example.title: Registering the App

title: package.json
overview: The package.json file stores information about your project, including its name, version, scripts, and dependencies. Whenever you install a library using npm or Yarn, it is automatically added to this file.

example.title: Installing a Library
example.content:
npm install axios

# or

yarn add axios

title: node_modules Folder
overview: The node_modules folder contains all the libraries and packages installed for your project. It is automatically generated after running npm install or yarn install. Since it can be recreated at any time, it is usually not committed to version control.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You have learned the purpose of the main folders and files in a React Native CLI project, including the android and ios folders, App.tsx, index.js, package.json, and node_modules. Understanding these files will make it easier to navigate and maintain React Native projects.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ android → Android project
✔ ios → iOS project
✔ App.tsx → Root component
✔ index.js → Entry point
✔ package.json → Project configuration
✔ node_modules → Installed dependencies
